MOVED BY:        COUNCILLOR SAHLSTROM
SECONDED:        COUNCILLOR SZPAK


         That Council approve the agenda with the addition of item 10 a), Town of View Royal, Re: Review
         of the Policy to Release Violent and/or Repeat Offenders.

3.       PUBLIC HEARING


         a)   BYLAW NO. 1896
              "Langford Official Community Plan Bylaw, Amendment No. 37, (2981 & 2985
              Awsworth Rd), Bylaw No. 1896, 2021".

              BYLAW NO. 1897
              "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 587, (2981 & 2985 Awsworth Rd), Bylaw
              No. 1897, 2021".

                                                                                                       August 16, 2021
                                                                                                          Page 2 of 22


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw Nos. 1896and 1897at 5:33 pm.

Deputy Director of Leah Stohmann advised that Susan Gale Wilson has applied to amend the Official
Community Plan designation of 2981 and 2985 Awsworth Road from "Hillside or Shoreline" to "Business or
Light Industrial" and "Agriculture", and to amend the text of the Rural Residential 4 Zone to allow a Truck
Terminal Facility at 2981 and 2985 Awsworth Road.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of truck terminal facility.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

    1. That prior to Bylaw Adoption, the applicant registers a Section 219 Covenant, in priorityof all other
       charges on title that agrees to the following prior to the issuance of a building permit:
                a. To provide and implement a stormwater management plan;
                b. To provide a Fire Underwriters Survey (FUS);
                c. To connect the building to the municipal sanitary sewer system within 6 months of a
                   sewer main being installed in a highway or City statutory right of way abutting the parcel;

                d. To pay the Sewer Capital Recovery Fee (SCRF) to West Shore Environmental Services or
                     the City of Langford;

                e. To install all on-site plumbing necessary between the building and a point 1.0 m from
                   the boundary of the highway or statutory right of way that the City designates as the
                   future location of the sewer, in accordance with the requirements of the City;

                f.   To applyfor a Form and Character Development Permit for any buildings constructed on
                     site that relate to the business use;

        2. And that prior to the Bylaw Adoption, the applicant shall provide a $5,000 bond for the
            construction of a fence along the boundary of the RR4 and AGl zone to delineate the land within
            the Agricultural Land Reserve to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning.

This proposal is consistent with the proposed Official Community Plan designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Val Creed. 3445 Luxton Road - Supports application for truck facility.

Susan Wilson, applicant - Here to answer any questions.

Anita Miller, 653 Seedtree Road - Fully support proposal, prime location for a truck facility, and barn needs
to come down as it's unsafe.

                                                                                                     August 16, 2021
                                                                                                         Page 3 of 22


Laurie Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Terrace - The OCP and zoning bylaw are changed too often, there should be
more limits on the uses. Signage should be better placed to ensure the public is notified. This property is
above an aquifer. TUP is good for two more years, should not be rezoned yet.

Joel Hanicka, 670 Mountainview Avenue - Support this proposal, as a heavy-duty mechanic apprentice for
Todd Wilson. The barn is ready to fall down, a proper facility is needed.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

Glen Creed - Lives in the neighbourhood, support application. Need more parking in the West Shore for
these trucks.


Pat Carvello - Supports the application.


Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the Public Hearing
for Bylaw Nos. 1896 and 1897 closed at 5:46 p.m.

        b)       BYLAW NO. 1912
                 "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 592, (925 and 929 Bray Ave), Bylaw No.
                 1912, 2021".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1912 at 5:46 pm.

Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Rachael Sansom has applied on behalf of
Rejuvenate Downtown Langford Nominee Incorporated to amend the zoning of 925 and 929 Bray Avenue
from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) Zone to the City Centre 1 (CCl) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a residential building with a maximum height
of 6-storeys.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to the following:

a) That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant provides the following contributions per residential
   unit prior to issuance of a building permit:
           i.    $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
          ii.    $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund, subject to permitted reductions in
                    accordance with the applicable Policy; and
          iii.      $10.75 per m^ of commercial Gross Floor Area towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

 b) That the applicant provides, prior to bylaw adoption, a section 219 covenant that agrees to the
    following:
         i.  To install all required frontage improvements, servicing upgrades, and any recommendations
             from the Traffic Impact Assessment, all to Bylaw 1000 standards;
        ii.  To provide and implement a storm water management plan;

                                                                                                         August 16, 2021
                                                                                                             Page 4 of 22


        iii.    To provide a construction parking management plan;
        iv.     To provide driveway access that aligns with Knotty Pine Road;
           V.   That parking stalls are allocated to individual units;
        vi.     That a Fire Underwriters Survey and a Fire Safety Plan are provided; and
       vii.     That a strata plan of the building is registered priorto occupancy.

 c) The applicant has provided the following prior to this Public Hearing, as required by Council:

           i.   Frontage drawings, a traffic impact assessment, and a stormwater management memo, all to
                the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Rachel Sansom, Represents Owners - Introduced development.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

Dana Elizabeth - Resident homeowner and businessperson in Langford. Support density and affordable
housing.

Mayor Young called a third time for speakers.

Sally Boulevant, 2867 Rita Road - Lives near Bray. Not in support of a condo building, feels like residents
are getting pushed out. Nothing is becoming more affordable. Parking concerns, this will cause more
parking on the side streets.

Gary Brown, 1319 Ravensview Drive - Support this project, more units and density.

Bernadette Armstrong, 2813 Rodney Road - Glad this is a condo and not a rental building. Traffic concerns
on Bray, Costin, Carlow. Difficult to get onto Leigh road, there should be a traffic light at one of the
intersections. Interchange needs more signage for park, perhaps flashing lights. Will water lines be
increased to the development, so it doesn't impact the neighbourhood?

Mike Wignall, 866 Goldstream Avenue - Support development, all about accommodating people who want
to move to Langford, and providing affordable housing.

Jacqueline Gintaut, 1331 Ravensview Drive - Concerned about size and scope of project, as well as traffic
and parking, we don't have the infrastructure for this. Please address the community's concerns. Needs
community consultation.

Mayor Young responded to questions.

Scott Emerv, 2866 Rita Road - Opposed to density, traffic and parking are getting worse.

                                                                                                        August 16, 2021
                                                                                                           Page 5 of 22


Sally Boulevant. 2867 Rita Road - Parking is one of the biggest concerns. There are 4 potential projects
going on in a small area and there is not enough parking.

Nadia Hood. 273 Lone Oak Place - Supports this project and affordable housing.

Ryan Alden. 845 Orono Avenue - Supports project, we need affordable housing.

Jaqueline Gintaut, 1331 Ravensview Drive - It is relevant for speakers to address nearby developments.
Condos aren't necessarily affordable - need public consultation. There was no broad public consultation
for OCP. Want to speak directly with elected officials.

Darlene Younger. 119 St Clair Boulevard - Support this project, need affordable housing.

Matthew McKay, 784 Hocklev Avenue - Support development, parking has been fine where density has
increased.


Ken Rant, 2145 Triangle Trail - Support this development, kids will need housing.

Ryan Craycroft, 3431 Luxton Road - This is a good project for the community.

Dylan Durance, 2689 Ernhill Drive - Support development.

Reece Harry, 3090 Shoreview Drive - Support downtown densification.


Brad Weatherall - Need affordable housing, support development.

Sally Boulevant, at 2867 Rita Road - Can you clarify whether this is affordable housing.

Mayor Young - Clarified that this was affordable housing.

Sally Boulevant - The project at the corner of Jacklin and Bray is not an affordable housing project.

Mayor Young - This is not an affordable housing project under the CRD or any government, this is private
investment funds to provide housing in the condo market. There will not be low-cost housing in this
building, but it will provide a lower cost alternative to buying a single-family home.

Resident at 3240 Woodruff Road - In support of this project, in need of housing in a central location.

Jacqueline Gintaut, Ravensview Drive - Wants broad-based community consultation and for issues to be
addressed.


Mayor Young called a fourth and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the Public Hearing
for Bylaw No. 1912 closed at 6:23 p.m.

        c)   BYLAW NO. 1956
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 616, (905, 909, 913, 917, 921 Bray
             Avenue, and 2884, 2886 Jacklin Road), Bylaw No. 1956, 2021".

                                                                                                      August 16, 2021
                                                                                                         Page 6 of 22


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1956 at 6:24 pm.

Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Rachael Sansom has applied on behalf of
Rejuvenate Downtown Langford Nominee Incorporated to amend the zoning of2884 Jacklin Road and 905,
909, 913, 917, and 921 Bray Avenue from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) Zone to the City Centre
Pedestrian (CCP) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development ofa mixed-use residential building.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to the following:

        a) That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant provides the following contributions per
              residential unit prior to issuance of a building permit:
                  i.   $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                  ii.   $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund, subjectto permitted reductions in
                        accordance with the applicable Policy; and
                iii.    $10.75 per m^ of commercial Gross Floor Area towards the General Amenity Reserve
                        Fund.


 b) That the applicant provides, prior to bylaw adoption, a section 219 covenant that agrees to the
     following:
               That no Development Permit be issued until lot consolidation has occurred;
               That at least 5% of the lot area be outdoor amenity space;
               That the applicant will install all required frontage improvements, provide, and implement a
               storm water management plan, and provide a construction parking management plan;
        iv.    That parking stalls are allocated to individual units;
        V.     That residential parkingstalls are provided with Level 2 charging capabilities;
        vi.    That a strata plan of the building is registered prior to occupancy; and
       vii.    That buildings west of the east side of Knotty Pine be limited in heightto 6 storeys;

c) The applicant has provided the following prior to this Public Hearing, as required by Council:

         i.    Frontage drawings, a traffic impact assessment, and a stormwater management memo, all to
               the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

This proposal isconsistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Tanner Hansom, 917 Bray Avenue - Lives in one of the buildings set to be demolished. Already lives with
complete strangers in order to be able to afford to live in Langford. A youth support worker, an essential
worker; roommates are essential workers. This development will displace children and essential workers.

                                                                                                      August 15, 2021
                                                                                                         Page 7 of 22



The landlord did not notify the tenants of this.

Rachel Sansom - Community was informed, notices went to the surrounding neighbourhood.

Bernadette Armstrong. 2813 Rodney Road - Don't know height of the proposed development. There are 2
cars per home, cars are clogging our roads, infrastructure is not keeping up.

Leah Stohmann, Deputy Director of Planning and Subdivision - Clarified height and parking requirements.
There is 1 visitor parking space required for every 4 units.

Laurie Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Terrace - This is a big change from 1 and 2 family residential, should require
plans at this point in the proposal.

Dylan MacLean, 1063 Costin Avenue - Support this development.

Rachel Sansom - Difficult to provide renderings at this point.

Dana Elizabeth. 2850 Aldwynd Road - Support condos over rentals. Electric vehicle chargers are good.

Scott Emery, 2866 Rita Road - Against the rezoning - not enough information.

Jacqueline Gintaut, 1331 Ravensview Drive - Need more than 1 parking spot per unit, we already have traffic
issues.


Laurie Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Terrace - Don't understand details likefloor space ratio, probably the majority
of residents don't either.


Alan Churchill, 658 Atkins Road - We don't know how many units there are. It appears that there are too
many issues with this application to approve rezoning. This many new residents will increase demand for
doctors and schools.


Sally Boulevant. 2867 Rita Road - Concerns about height, there should be a maximum height. Don't think it's
possible to accommodate necessary parking.

Alison Gettis, 3311 Mesa Place - Do not support, too much traffic and congestion.

Tanner Hansom. 917 Bray Avenue - Do we know the approximate cost to won one of these condos. Working
48 hours per week and can't afford a studio.

Rachel Sansom - Available to answer any questions.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

Mike Wignall, 866 Goldstream Avenue - The community is growing. We need to create density nodes.
Regional growth strategy identifies the West Shore as a place for this growth. Support this application.

Councillor Blackwell left the meeting at 6:53 pm.

                                                                                                          August 16, 2021
                                                                                                              Page 8 of 22


Brianna Champagne. 917 Bray Avenue - Disapproves ofthis application. Will be displaced, and can't afford
replacement housing, have to live w/ith roommates in orderto afford living here.

Jeff Heslop, 905 Bray Avenue - Need a 4-bedroom rental home that allows pets. Need housing that fits
larger/blended families. Current condos and apartments in the area do not fit larger families. Can't find any
rentals.


Sarah Desone, 905 Bray Avenue-If this application goes through, will have to leave yet another home. There
are no houses available for largerfamilies. Not in support of this application. This will uproot 13 families and
their children.


Councillor Blackwell returned to the meeting at 6:55 pm.

Jacqueline Gintaut, 1331 Ravensview Drive- Procedural concerns about speakingat meetings.

MayorYoung called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the Public Hearing
for Bylaw No. 1956 closed at 7:00 p.m.

                "Langford Official Community Plan Bylaw, Amendment No. 43, (3553 and 3559

                BYLAW NO. 1986
                "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 629, (3553 and 3559 Happy Valley Rd),
                Bylaw No. 1986, 2021".

scale commercial uses.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

    l.That the applicant agrees to provide, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the following:
            a. Asubdivision plan that consolidates the two subject properties and includes road dedication,
                   to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering
                b. AStatutory Right of Way (SRW) in favour of the City of Langford on the northwest corner at
                   the intersection to allow a stormwater culvert to be installed

                                                                                                             Page 9 of 22


             c.   A Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title that agrees to the
                  following;
                       i. That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards

                                   1. frontage improvements, including but not limited to separated

             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 631, (#136-1047 Langford Pkwy), Bylaw
             No. 1991, 2021".

        f)   BYLAW NO. 1994
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 634, (648, 652, 656, 660 Granderson
             Road), Bylaw No. 1994, 2021".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1994 at 7:03 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Stew Gordon of Gordon n Gordon Interiors Ltd. Has
applied to amendthe zoning of 648, 652, 656, and 660Granderson Road from the R2 (One- and Two-Family
Residential) Zone to the CCl (City Centre 1) Zone.

This is being proposed inorder to allow for the developmentof a six-storey building containing approximately
84 apartment units.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
    residential unit, prior to the issuance of a building permit:
        a. $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
        b. $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
             Subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the Affordable
             Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.

2. That the applicant provides, prior to bylaw adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of all
    other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

        a.   That the following are provided to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director
             of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building Permit:
                  i. Frontage improvements;
                 ii. A storm water management plan; and
                iii. A construction parking and traffic management plan;

        b. That parking stalls are allocated to individual units;
        c. That residential parking stalls are provided with Level 2 charging capabilities;

        d. That a strata plan of the building is registered prior to occupancy;

                                                                                                      August 16, 2021
                                                                                                        Page 11 of 22


        e. Acknowledgement that the site is in proximity to an existing rail corridor that may be utilized for
           transportation uses in the future such as, but not limited to rail, bus, or other, that these uses
           may result in general nuisances, and that the owner and all future owners assume all risk and
            annoyance of such nuisances;

3. The applicant has provided the following prior to this Public Hearing, as required by Council:
      a. Frontage drawings to confirm that road dedication is not required, a traffic impact assessment,
            and a stormwater management memo, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Colby Messer, 2149 Triangle Trail - Represent owners. We need density now in order to get better public
transportation. Construction parking will be managed. Affordable housing is needed.

Tyler Lister, 2958 Brock Place - Support project, more development will help small businesses and improve
neighbourhood.

Rob LeClair, 1323 Ravensview Drive - Supports development which provides affordable housing, good for
retirees and young families.

Melissa Olsen, 933 Latoria Road - Supports this project.

Rael Patterson, 929 Latoria Road - Supports this project.

George Wetherall, 925 Latoria Road - Supports project.

Dylan McLean, 1063 Costin Avenue - Supports development.

Nadia Hood, 273 Lone Oak Place - Supports project.

Ryan Oldman, 845 Orono Avenue - Supports project, need affordable housing in city core.

Brad Weatherall, 1015 Torrence Avenue - Supports project.

Reece Harry, 3090 Shoreview Drive - Supports project.

Melinda Courser-Supports project.

Resident at 3240 Woodruff Road - Supports project.

Brandon Storey, 1051 Englewood Avenue - Supports project.

Dylan Durance, 2689 Hernell Drive - Supports proiect.


David Mullen. 662 Goldstream Avenue - Does not support project, will increase traffic problems.

                                                                                                      August 16, 2021
                                                                                                         Page 12 of 22


Ken Rant - Supports project. We need more affordable housing for young people in the market.

Cheryl Gervais. 3579 Happy Valley Road - Supports project.

Jody Twa. 2320 Lairds Gate - Good choice, great location next to E&N corridor.

Alan Churchill, 658 Atkins Avenue - Will overlook houses, concerned about traffic issues. When
developments are considered one at a time, overall planning may be lacking. What is the goal density?

city centre in particular, we have overall growth projections for Langford as a whole. The housing needs
report is on the Langford website.

Alan Churchill - We need more schools and doctors to support density.

Mayor Young - Langford is proactive in recruiting doctors, but Island Health and the Provincial Government

                                                                                                      August 16, 2021
                                                                                                        Page 13 of 22

allowed_new_decisions.operative_body: That Council approve the minutes of the regular meeting of Council held on July 19, 2021, and the special meeting of Council on July 29, 2021.
That Council receive the minutes of the Planning, Zoning and Affordable Housing Committee held on August 9, 2021.

That Council: 1. Direct staff to provide notice that Council will consider issuing amended Temporary Use Permits for the following properties: #105 693 Hoffman Ave (TUP19-0001 - Clarity Cannabis), #101 945 Reunion Ave (TUP19-0002 - The Original Farm), #107 2317 Millstream Rd (TUP19-0004 - Honeycomb Cannabis) and #101 977 Langford Pkwy (TUP20-0002 - Flight Cannabis), to allow for the following: a) To amend the operating hours as follows, 9am to 9pm Sunday through Wednesday and 9am to 10pm Thursday through Saturday; b) To increase the permitted signage from two signs to three signs subject to the regulations in Bylaw 1250.
That Council give Bylaw No. 1896 second and third readings.
That Council give Bylaw No. 1897 second and third readings.
That Council give Bylaw No. 1912 second and third readings.
That Council give Bylaw No. 1956 second and third readings.
That Council give Bylaw No. 1981 first reading.
That Council give Bylaw No. 1985 second and third readings.
That Council give Bylaw No. 1986 second and third readings.
That Council give Bylaw No. 1991 second and third readings.
That Council give Bylaw No. 1994 second and third readings.

That Council direct staff to draft a letter supporting the City of Victoria and the Town of View Royal in requesting a review of the policy to release violent and/or repeat offenders awaiting charged disposition, in support of our West Shore RCMP.

THAT Council close the meeting to the public pursuant to section 90 (1) c, e, and g of the Community Charter to consider: • Labour relations or other employee relations; • the acquisition, disposition or expropriation of land or improvements, if the council considers that disclosure could reasonably be expected to harm the interests of the municipality; • litigation or potential litigation affecting the municipality.
